documents.title: Academic Integrity (Student Handbook policy)
documents.stance_why: The only AI passage says use 'outside of the bounds established by the instructor and/or course syllabus' counts as academic dishonesty, so the bounds come from instructors and the document itself neither bans nor permits AI; this is delegation.
documents.summary: The Student Handbook academic-integrity policy brings generative AI use under existing academic dishonesty rules when it falls outside the bounds an instructor or syllabus sets. It sets no AI rule of its own, tells students to ask instructors, and leaves penalties and case handling to the instructor within a general misconduct procedure.

units.why: The sentence states that AI use 'outside of the bounds established by the instructor and/or course syllabus' falls under the academic dishonesty designations, so improper AI use is misconduct. It binds students during work, so P36 fits better than P04, which concerns who decides.
units.anchor: outside of the bounds established by the instructor and/or course syllabus, shall also fall underneath
units.frag_start: The use of generative artificial intelligence
units.policy: Use of generative AI tools in student-created work outside the bounds established by the instructor and/or course syllabus falls under the academic dishonesty designations.

units.why: The same sentence makes the instructor and syllabus the source of the AI bounds ('established by the instructor and/or course syllabus'); the university sets no default itself. P04 fits because the decision is left to each instructor or syllabus.
units.anchor: bounds established by the instructor and/or course syllabus
units.frag_start: The use of generative artificial intelligence
units.policy: The bounds on generative AI use in student work are established by the instructor and/or the course syllabus.

units.why: The sentence says 'Students are expected to consult their instructors if they have any questions about the use of AI tools', which tells students who are unsure to ask first; that is P10.
units.anchor: Students are expected to consult their instructors if they have any questions about the use

units.why: The opening defines integrity as 'ensuring that all ideas and work presented are your own'. It does not mention AI but is the standard the AI sentence imports, and it says submitted work must be the student's own, so P29.
units.anchor: ensuring that all ideas and work presented are your own
units.fit_note: Stated for all academic work, not AI specifically; applies to AI only through the later designation sentence.

units.why: The policy says 'The academic integrity policy applies to all students, undergraduate and graduate, and to scholarly pursuits and research', which sets scope; with the AI sentence it covers AI in research too. P62 is nearest but fits only partly.
units.anchor: applies to all students, undergraduate and graduate, and to scholarly pursuits and research
units.fit_note: A general scope of the integrity policy to research; does not mention AI in research or defer to venue rules.

units.why: The text says violations will be addressed 'in an effective and educational manner' with the instructor deciding case by case; this covers AI violations since they fall under these designations. The educational framing is P68.
units.anchor: will be addressed in an effective and educational manner
units.frag_start: It is taken seriously at RPI
units.fit_note: Phrase is brief and general to all academic dishonesty, not tied to first offenses or AI.

units.why: The policy lists penalties: 'the instructor may require the student to redo the assignment for a reduced grade, assign the student a failing grade for the assignment'. These are concrete penalties for dishonesty, which includes out-of-bounds AI use, so P37.
units.anchor: redo the assignment for a reduced grade, assign the student a failing grade
units.frag_start: Within a class, the instructor may
units.policy: The instructor may require the student to redo the assignment for a reduced grade, assign a failing grade for the assignment, assign a failing grade for the class, or terminate participation in a research project.
units.fit_note: Penalties are stated for all academic dishonesty, not AI specifically.

units.why: The policy lists disciplinary actions ('warning, probation, suspension, expulsion') that follow a 'judicial inquiry'; these are concrete sanctions for dishonesty including AI misuse, so P37.
units.anchor: warning, probation, suspension, expulsion, and/or alternative actions as agreed on by the student
units.fit_note: Disciplinary sanctions are stated for all academic dishonesty, not AI specifically.

units.why: The policy bars students found responsible from dropping the course: 'prohibited from dropping a course to avoid the academic penalty'. It is an additional consequence of a finding, so P37.
units.anchor: prohibited from dropping a course to avoid the academic penalty
units.fit_note: A procedural consequence (no drop, no grade-option change) rather than a grade penalty; general to all dishonesty.

units.why: The instructor 'will contact the student(s) about alleged misconduct and schedule a meeting to discuss the allegations' within ten business days, so the instructor talks with the student before deciding, which is P57.
units.anchor: contact the student(s) about alleged misconduct and schedule a meeting to discuss the allegations
units.frag_end: of having discovered the possible dishonesty.
units.fit_note: A mandatory meeting for any suspected dishonesty with a ten-day deadline, not AI specific.

units.why: The instructor will 'review the circumstances and evidence' and 'allow the student the opportunity to provide their perspective', which gives the accused student a right to respond: P64.
units.anchor: allow the student the opportunity to provide their perspective on the situation
units.fit_note: Stated for all academic dishonesty cases, not AI specifically.

units.why: The passage has the instructor review the situation and speak 'with others who might be involved or have knowledge of the situation' before determining the violation, which sets how a finding is reached; nearest type is P69 though no standard of proof is given.
units.anchor: speaking with others who might be involved or have knowledge of the situation
units.frag_end: extent of the violation, if any, by the accused student.
units.fit_note: Describes steps for gathering evidence but states no standard or kinds of evidence insufficient.

units.why: The written decision must include 'information regarding the student's option to appeal the grade decision', which gives students a route to contest a finding (P64) in cases that include AI.
units.anchor: information regarding the student's option to appeal the grade decision
units.frag_end: time limit in which to do so.
units.fit_note: Concerns notification of appeal rights after the decision, not responding to allegations; general to all dishonesty.

units.why: Instructors who apply a sanction 'must complete the Academic Integrity Violation Report Form' within a week, and the incident is kept on file 'to track repeat or multiple offenses'. This is an enforcement record rule that fits no listed type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: must complete the Academic Integrity Violation Report Form on the Dean of Students website
units.frag_end: repeat or multiple offenses by the same student(s).
units.uncovered_note: Instructors must file a violation report with the Dean of Students office, which keeps a record to track repeat offenses.

units.why: The instructor 'can request that formal judicial action be taken against a student in addition to the established academic penalty', with referral to the Director of Student Rights; this escalation route has no matching type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: the instructor can request that formal judicial action be taken against a student
units.uncovered_note: Instructors may escalate a dishonesty case to formal judicial action on top of the grade penalty.

units.why: A student 'can submit a written appeal of an academic penalty to the Department Head' within five business days, with further levels to the Dean and Provost. It gives accused students a way to contest penalties (P64), covering AI cases.
units.anchor: a student can submit a written appeal of an academic penalty to the Department Head
units.fit_note: A multi-level appeal ladder for penalties, not a right to respond to the allegation itself.

documents.title: Generative AI Policy
documents.stance_why: The captured text states only a purpose, 'to establish guidelines for use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) at Rensselaer', for information security; it sets no rule on student AI use in teaching, so the stance is delegates by default.
documents.summary: Only the Policy Library landing page was captured; it states the policy's purpose as guidelines for generative AI use that keep Rensselaer compliant with information security and privacy policies and safeguard institutional data. The policy document itself is not in the text, so no classroom stance can be read from it.

units.why: The page says the policy exists 'to establish guidelines for use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) at Rensselaer', an institution-level statement of purpose and scope, so P56.
units.anchor: establish guidelines for use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) at Rensselaer

units.why: The purpose is to keep AI use in 'compliance with existing over-arching policies on information security and privacy'; this ties AI use to existing university policy, so P77 rather than P50, which needs an instruction to protect data or use vetted tools.
units.anchor: maintain compliance with existing over-arching policies on information security and privacy

units.why: The purpose also includes to 'safeguard institutional data', a data-protection aim for AI use, so P50 fits partly; the page gives no concrete rule, so it is informs.
units.fit_note: States the aim of protecting institutional data only; no instruction about personal data or vetted tools.

notes: The Generative AI Policy PDF was not retrievable; only the landing page purpose is coded. The DOSO document has one AI sentence; the remaining units are general academic-integrity procedure that the AI sentence brings into scope (coded with fit_notes). RPI syllabus guidance was inaccessible; no computing-unit policy found.
